text.text_excerpt: Tastee Restaurant is as close as you're going to get to McKenzie's unless you've got a time machine. New Orleans is a unique place. If you ask someone where they went to school and they answer with anything other than their high school, they aren't a local. It's not that we don't appreciate our colleges, but those dont really tell someone anything about you. Similarly we equate childhood memories with food even when the place that served it has vanished from the landscape. Many of my favorite childhood memories involved trips to McKenzie's to but pastries, cakes or cookies. I vividly remember my dad picking up turtles for my mom or my mom taking us to get treats during the summer or days ...

I'm so damned biased on this review; I won't lie. As a New Orleans native, this bakery has preserved a big part of my childhood. It almost brings me to tears when I think about the day the McKenzie's chain of bakeries closed, due to political gobbledegoop with the city. Products: It would take entirely too long to go over everything available here, but for old-timers like myself, you probably know most of the menu by heart. The crown jewel for me here is the buttermilk drop---that wonderful glazed lump of deep fried yellow cake batter, colored a golden brown. They get the flavor spot-on here. The only thing weird for me is that this place makes them uniform, with I assume a batter dispens...

This Tastee is a neighborhood favorite for lots of reasons. They're conveniently located smack, dab, in the middle of Lakeview. They serve a pretty wide variety of breakfast options. Doughnuts, breakfast sandwiches, sliders, breakfast platters and lots of pastries. The service is quick and friendly too. My only issues are the breakfast biscuits. They are usually over done. If you stick with doughnuts, you really can't go wrong, and if you're looking for desserts, they've got some good ones too - turtles, black out cake, the ever popular jelly roll, and the cinnamon rolls that some of us remember from our McKenzie's days. They're all there. I almost forgot about their buttermilk drops. OMG...
